body:
`helper.save_cover_from_filestorage` opens the final target (`<book path>/cover.jpg`) with
`wb` and writes into it. A disk-full, a short write, or an interrupted network-share write
therefore truncates a previously valid cover, with no backup and no way back.

Every cover-write surface shares this: the classic editor's upload, the cover picker's apply,
the SPA's `POST /api/v1/books/<id>/cover`, and the ingest auto-metadata fetch. The same shape
also makes the whole operation non-transactional — the file is replaced BEFORE the database
commit, so a commit failure leaves new bytes on disk with old `has_cover`/`last_modified`.

Smallest fix: write to a temporary sibling on the same filesystem, validate it, then
`os.replace()` into position after the metadata transaction succeeds; keep the previous file
until the rename lands so a failure can be compensated. Google Drive needs the equivalent.

Found by an adversarial review of PR #1739. Deliberately NOT fixed there: it is shared by every
cover path and is a restructuring of the write, not of the caching that PR is about.
title: Cover writes replace the library file in place with no staging, so an I/O failure destroys the old cover
